question: In nursing students, is virtual reality-based teaching more effective than traditional or alternative teaching methods for improving theoretical knowledge, practical skills, skill retention, satisfaction, and critical thinking?
eligibility: Participants are nursing students in a nursing education programme (undergraduate/pre-registration or postgraduate).
The intervention delivers education or training through virtual reality, immersive simulation, or a virtual patient/environment.
Comparison against traditional/conventional teaching or an alternative (e.g. non-immersive) instructional method.
Reports at least one learning outcome: knowledge, practical/clinical skills, skill retention, satisfaction, self-efficacy, or critical thinking.
A randomized controlled trial or otherwise controlled comparative educational intervention.
source: Health-professions (nursing) education systematic review + meta-analysis: Liu et al., 'Effectiveness of virtual reality in nursing education', BMC Med Educ 2023;23:710 (PMID 37770884, doi 10.1186/s12909-023-04662-x). Education-adjacent-health topic chosen for PubMed reachability; gold = 6/12 included RCTs that are MEDLINE-indexed (6 Chinese-language included studies are PubMed-unreachable).
notes: Converted from the protocol-first branch. naive_blocks come from protocols written by the fixture author, some tightened while looking at the gold set, so the naive floor may be optimistic.
